modelAnswer: Data analytics is the process of examining data to find patterns and draw conclusions, while data science is a broader interdisciplinary field using mathematics, statistics and machine learning to extract knowledge from data. They are related but different: data analytics is one activity within the larger scope of data science.

modelAnswer: Data science helps businesses analyze customer behavior, forecast sales, detect fraud and optimize operations by finding patterns and insights hidden in large volumes of business data.

modelAnswer: Machine learning uses algorithms that learn patterns from data with some human-selected features (like a student following a structured formal course), while deep learning uses artificial neural networks that learn features on their own directly from raw data (more like open-ended, informal, self-directed learning).

modelAnswer: Summary statistics (mean, median, range, etc.) condense a large dataset into a few meaningful numbers, making it easier to quickly understand the data's central tendency and spread without examining every value.

modelAnswer: Data storage preserves data safely so it can be retrieved, analyzed and reused later, forming the foundation that data analytics, machine learning and reporting all depend on.

keyPoints: Data science combines mathematics, statistics, data analysis and machine learning to extract knowledge and insight from data.

modelAnswer: Data science combines mathematics, statistics, data analysis, and machine learning to turn data into knowledge and insights. Its key concepts include collecting data, analyzing it for patterns, and using the resulting insights to make informed decisions about real-world problems such as healthcare, education, research, and business.

modelAnswer: A database is an organized system for storing, managing and retrieving data, usually supporting many datasets, while a dataset is a specific, structured or processed collection of data tied to one particular body of work.
stem: Differentiate between database and dataset.

keyPoints: Qualitative/categorical data labels objects into groups (e.g. colors), while quantitative/numerical data is measured in numbers.
Within categorical data, ordinal data has a meaningful order (e.g. grades) while nominal data does not (e.g. names).
Within numerical data, discrete data takes only fixed countable values, while continuous data can take any value within a range.
modelAnswer: Data in data science is broadly qualitative (categorical) or quantitative (numeric). Qualitative data labels objects or groups and includes ordinal data, which has an order or ranking, and nominal data, which has no meaningful order. Quantitative data uses numeric values and includes discrete data, which is countable and takes fixed values, and continuous data, which can take measurements between realistic points.
stem: Develop your own thinking on the various data types used in data science.

modelAnswer: Big data refers to datasets too large and complex for traditional tools to process easily. For an email box with hundreds of emails: Volume is the total number of emails stored, Velocity is the rate new emails arrive, and Variety is the mix of formats (text, attachments, images) within those emails.
stem: Express big data in your own words. Explain the three V's of big data with reference to email data. (Hint: An email box that contains hundreds of emails)

keyPoints: Healthcare: analyzing patient records to predict disease outbreaks or personalize treatment.
Business/retail: analyzing purchase history to recommend products and forecast demand.
Transportation: analyzing traffic and GPS data to optimize routes and reduce congestion.
modelAnswer: Big data is applicable wherever large volumes of data can reveal patterns that support better decisions. In healthcare, wearable devices and sensors feed patient data into electronic health records so providers can predict outbreaks and health risks. In media and entertainment, organizations analyze viewer patterns to target audiences and advertisements. In manufacturing, big data supports better products, fault tracking, supply planning, and energy efficiency. Governments can use analytics to understand citizens' needs, reduce costs, improve services, and combat fraud.
stem: Compare how big data is applicable to various fields of life. Illustrate your answer with suitable examples.

keyPoints: Advantages: better decision-making, discovering hidden patterns, and personalizing services at scale.
Challenges: storing and processing the sheer volume, ensuring data quality/variety is handled correctly, and protecting privacy and security.
Both sides stem from the same three V's (Volume, Velocity, Variety) that define big data.
modelAnswer: Big data helps individuals, organizations, and businesses optimize work and develop cost-effective solutions. Its benefits include anticipating customer demand, predictive maintenance, improved customer satisfaction, fraud detection, and stronger cybersecurity. Its challenges include poor data quality that can produce misleading insights, protecting privacy and security in massive datasets, rapid data growth, selecting compatible tools, and integrating diverse data formats and structures.
stem: Relate the advantages and challenges of big data.

keyPoints: Hospitals collect huge volumes of patient records, imaging data and wearable-device readings (big data).
Data science techniques (machine learning models) analyze this data to predict disease risk early and recommend personalized treatment plans.
Result: faster diagnoses, reduced costs, and improved patient outcomes compared to traditional, manual record review.
modelAnswer: Case study: A hospital collects data from patients' wearable devices and sensors and feeds it in real time into electronic health records. Doctors analyze the combined data to identify patients at risk, predict epidemic outbreaks, issue alerts, and help prevent serious medical conditions. Researchers can also use the data to select treatments, study drug side effects, and forecast health risks. This replaces reliance on isolated records with evidence from large, current datasets and supports earlier, better-informed care.
stem: Design a case study about how data science and big data has revolutionized the field of healthcare.
